title: Using several fingers for a strong low note on gut strings
summary: With high action and gut strings he stacks three fingers behind the note for strength, both arco and pizzicato.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now you were showing me something too about how -- in order to play a note strongly, you use -- you were showing me how you put your fingers across the strings.

Yes. Well, in other words, if I were to make a note, so-called legitimately, like a B-flat, with my little finger, in some cases, I use all of my -- more or less put three fingers along with it and a couple of other fingers along with my little finger in order to give it more strength because of the fact that my strings are so -- quite a distance from my finger board and it makes it tense, very tense. And of course, the strings, they're fairly heavy. I'm still using gut strings and especially when I get down to the low A and the E-string, it's very tense. In order for me to sustain a low and decent bass note, I have to press real hard. So I use at least three fingers to back it up, like I'm playing a low G (plays note). If I only use one finger, it would make that (plays note), I couldn't quite hit that note like I want to because it's so tense, it's so far away from the finger board. I'm using one finger. Now I'm using three fingers
Now, would you play that and sing with it? (Inaudible).

Right. (Playing bass). And bring it up an octave, (playing bass.) You know, if I'm not singing (playing note.) That's an open G on my top string (plays note), which I don't have to finger, you know. But it's according to how much pressure I put on my bow also. (Playing bass). And let it ring.
Uh-huh. Now does that same thing hold true for pizzicato?
Would you give us an example?

In other words, if you want to play a low note when you pizzicato, I play a low G, I use three fingers to do it (plays note) so it can ring. Otherwise, if I use just one finger (plays note), it's kind of muffled-like and it's not putting enough strength onto it. And like I said before, my strings are quite a distance, I would say, almost a half-inch from my finger board down at the bottom of my finger board. That's something that I have worked on and worked out through the years. (Playing bass).
